optional_codes.reason: Occasional dysphagia is reported in the history and is not listed as a diagnosis. It is not required, and it is accepted if reported. Either answer is defensible.

citations.case: ICD-10-CM Tabular List FY2027, Excludes1 note at category K20 (esophagitis with gastro-esophageal reflux disease and reflux esophagitis are coded to K21.0-); ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines FY2027, Section I.A.15 ('with': the classification presumes a link between the two conditions, and here the provider also states it); Section I.B.5 (signs and symptoms integral to a definitive diagnosis are not coded separately); Section I.C.21.c.3 (Z79: long-term drug therapy codes are for long-term use and are not assigned for a drug given for a brief period)

coder_notes: The provider lists gastroesophageal reflux disease and esophagitis as two diagnoses and states the esophagitis is due to reflux; the EGD shows no bleeding. One combination code covers both. Los Angeles grade and the distal site have no code axis. Heartburn and regurgitation are integral to the diagnosis. Dysphagia is accepted but not required (see optional_codes). Omeprazole for 2 weeks is not long-term drug therapy and is not coded. The negative EGD findings are not coded. Traps: reporting a separate esophagitis code (K20.90) with the reflux code, against the Excludes1 note at K20; coding reflux without esophagitis; the with-bleeding code (K21.01)
